QuestionText: What does ISRO stand for?
Explanation: ISRO stands for Indian Space Research Organisation. It is India's national space agency, founded in 1969.

QuestionText: India's Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed on which part of the Moon?
Explanation: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's South Pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to do so.

QuestionText: Who is called the 'Missile Man of India'?
Explanation: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam is called the 'Missile Man of India' for his key role in developing India's missile programme (AGNI, PRITHVI).

QuestionText: Who founded India's space programme?
Explanation: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is considered the father of India's space programme. He established ISRO's predecessor INCOSPAR in 1962.

QuestionText: India's first satellite was named?
Explanation: Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched on 19 April 1975 by a Soviet rocket. It was named after the ancient Indian mathematician.

QuestionText: Who was India's first person to go to space?
Explanation: Rakesh Sharma went to space on 3 April 1984 aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11 spacecraft. When PM Indira Gandhi asked how India looked, he said 'Saare jahan se achcha'.

QuestionText: Who discovered the 'Raman Effect' in physics?
Explanation: Sir CV Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928, for which he won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.

QuestionText: Jagadish Chandra Bose is famous for inventing what?
Options: A) Radio (wireless communication) and researching plant life
Explanation: J.C. Bose is credited with pioneering wireless radio communication and proving that plants have life. He invented the crescograph.

QuestionText: India's nuclear programme was started under whose leadership?
Explanation: Homi Jehangir Bhabha is called the 'Father of India's Nuclear Programme'. He founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and BARC.

QuestionText: India launched its Mars mission 'Mangalyaan' in which year?
Explanation: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was launched in November 2013 and entered Mars orbit in September 2014.

QuestionText: India became the __ country to successfully reach Mars orbit.
Explanation: India became the 4th country (after USSR, USA, and the European Space Agency) to successfully reach Mars orbit with Mangalyaan.

QuestionText: The 'Aditya-L1' mission launched by ISRO studies which celestial body?
Explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's first solar mission, launched on 2 September 2023 to study the Sun from a halo orbit around Lagrange Point 1.

QuestionText: What is the name of ISRO's heavy rocket launcher?
Explanation: The GSLV Mark III (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mk III), also called LVM3, is ISRO's most powerful rocket.

QuestionText: What is the full form of PSLV?
Explanation: PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle. It is ISRO's most reliable rocket and has launched over 50 missions.

QuestionText: The Chandrayaan-1 mission discovered which important substance on the Moon?
Explanation: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) made the landmark discovery of water molecules on the lunar surface, confirmed by NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper instrument.

QuestionText: Srinivasa Ramanujan is famous for contributions in which field?
Explanation: Srinivasa Ramanujan was a self-taught mathematical genius from India. He made extraordinary contributions to number theory, infinite series, and continued fractions.

QuestionText: Who discovered that plants respond to stimuli like animals?
Explanation: Jagadish Chandra Bose demonstrated through experiments that plants respond to stimuli, effectively proving they have life similar to animals.

QuestionText: India's UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is managed by which organisation?
Options: A) NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India)
Explanation: UPI is managed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India). India leads the world in real-time digital payments through UPI.

QuestionText: The IIT (Indian Institutes of Technology) are premier institutions for which field?
Explanation: IITs are India's premier engineering and technology institutes. They produce world-class engineers and researchers.

QuestionText: What is Aadhaar?
Options: A) India's unique 12-digit biometric identity number system
Explanation: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number issued to residents of India, based on their biometric and demographic data. It is managed by UIDAI.

QuestionText: DRDO stands for?
Options: A) Defence Research and Development Organisation
B) Department of Research and Development
D) Digital Research and Design Office
Explanation: DRDO stands for Defence Research and Development Organisation. It develops military technology for India's defence forces.

QuestionText: India's first supercomputer was named?
Explanation: PARAM was India's first supercomputer, developed by C-DAC in 1991. PARAM 8000 put India among the top nations in supercomputing.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution in India'?
Explanation: M.S. Swaminathan is called the Father of Green Revolution in India for his role in developing high-yielding wheat varieties, transforming India from a food-deficient to food-surplus nation.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Father of White Revolution' (Operation Flood) in India?
Explanation: Verghese Kurien is called the Father of the White Revolution. He created Amul and led Operation Flood, making India the world's largest milk producer.

QuestionText: Which Indian scientist discovered the element responsible for the blue colour of the sky?
Options: A) CV Raman (Raman scattering explains it)
Explanation: CV Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect also helped explain the blue colour of the sea. The blue sky is explained by Rayleigh scattering, but Raman's work on light scattering is closely related.

QuestionText: The 'Bose-Einstein Condensate' is named after which Indian scientist?
Explanation: Satyendranath Bose collaborated with Albert Einstein on quantum statistics. This work led to the theory of Bose-Einstein Condensate, a new state of matter.

QuestionText: India's Gaganyaan mission aims to do what?
Options: A) Send Indian astronauts to space on an Indian rocket
Explanation: Gaganyaan is ISRO's crewed mission that aims to send three Indian astronauts (Gagannauts) into low Earth orbit for 3 days using an Indian rocket.

QuestionText: In which city is ISRO's headquarters located?
Explanation: ISRO's headquarters is in Bengaluru (Bangalore), Karnataka.

QuestionText: India's Vikram Lander (Chandrayaan-3) was named after which scientist?
Explanation: The Vikram Lander of Chandrayaan-3 is named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of India's space programme.

QuestionText: The 'Pragyaan' rover of Chandrayaan-3 moved on the Moon's surface and detected which element?
Explanation: The Pragyaan rover detected sulphur and several other elements on the Moon's south polar region using its LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) instrument.

QuestionText: India's first remote sensing satellite was named?
Explanation: IRS-1A (Indian Remote Sensing Satellite 1A) was launched in 1988. It was India's first dedicated earth observation/remote sensing satellite.

QuestionText: PARAM Siddhi-AI is India's most powerful AI supercomputer, built under which programme?
Explanation: PARAM Siddhi-AI was built under India's National Supercomputing Mission. It ranked 63rd in the TOP500 list of world's fastest supercomputers (2020).

QuestionText: Which Indian institution launched a nano-satellite built entirely by students?
Explanation: IIT Bombay's Pratham nano-satellite was designed and built by students and launched by ISRO in 2016 to measure Total Electron Content in the ionosphere.

QuestionText: The 'Rohini' satellite series was launched using which Indian-made rocket?
Explanation: The Rohini satellite was launched by India's own SLV-3 (Satellite Launch Vehicle) in 1980, marking India's first successful satellite launch with a domestic rocket.

QuestionText: India's NAVIC is India's own navigation satellite system. What does NavIC stand for?
Explanation: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is India's own GPS-like satellite navigation system with 7 satellites, giving positional accuracy of less than 20 metres.

QuestionText: Who invented the electronic voting machine (EVM) used in Indian elections?
Options: A) Electronics Corporation of India (ECIL) and BEL
Explanation: Electronic Voting Machines used in Indian elections were developed by ECIL (Electronics Corporation of India Limited) and BEL (Bharat Electronics Limited) in collaboration with the Election Commission.

QuestionText: Aryabhata — India's first satellite — was named after which ancient Indian scholar?
Explanation: Aryabhata (5th century CE) was a pioneering Indian mathematician and astronomer who calculated the value of pi and proposed that Earth rotates on its axis.

QuestionText: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) is located in which city?
Explanation: IISc (Indian Institute of Science) is in Bengaluru. It is India's premier research institution, founded in 1909 with support from Jamsetji Tata.

QuestionText: India's first nuclear test was called?
Explanation: India's first nuclear test was codenamed 'Smiling Buddha', conducted on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran in Rajasthan.

QuestionText: Which spacecraft from India was sent to study Venus?
Explanation: ISRO's Shukrayaan-1 is a planned Venus orbiter mission, expected to study Venus's atmosphere and geological features.

QuestionText: C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing) is best known for developing?
Explanation: C-DAC developed India's PARAM series of supercomputers, starting with PARAM 8000 in 1991, putting India among the world's top nations in supercomputing.

QuestionText: What is the name of India's scientific research station in Antarctica?
Explanation: India has two active Antarctic research stations: Maitri (since 1989) and Bharati (since 2012). Dakshin Gangotri was the first (1983) but is now buried under ice.

QuestionText: BARC stands for?
Options: D) Board of Atomic Research & Chemistry
Explanation: BARC (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre) is India's premier nuclear research facility in Trombay, Mumbai. It is named after Homi Bhabha.

QuestionText: India's digital payments app BHIM is named after?
Explanation: BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) is named in honour of Dr. BR Ambedkar. It uses UPI for instant bank-to-bank payments.

QuestionText: The first indigenously developed vaccine against COVID-19 in India was?
Explanation: Covaxin was India's first indigenously developed COVID-19 vaccine, developed by Bharat Biotech in collaboration with ICMR and NIV.

QuestionText: What does SAT (IRNSS) satellites help with?
Options: A) Navigation and positioning in India and nearby region
Explanation: India's IRNSS (Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System), also called NavIC, provides accurate positioning and navigation services in India and up to 1,500 km beyond its borders.

QuestionText: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SHAR) — ISRO's launch facility — is located in?
Explanation: ISRO's main launch centre is the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. It is on an island off the Bay of Bengal.

QuestionText: India's Operation Flood (White Revolution) made India the world's largest producer of?
Explanation: Operation Flood, led by Verghese Kurien and NDDB, transformed India into the world's largest milk producer through the cooperative dairy model pioneered by Amul.

QuestionText: Which satellite network does India use for direct-to-home television broadcasting?
Explanation: The INSAT (Indian National Satellite System) series of geostationary satellites are used for television broadcasting, weather forecasting, and telecommunications in India.

QuestionText: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) was founded by which scientist?
Explanation: Homi Jehangir Bhabha founded TIFR in 1945 with the support of the Tata Trust. It is India's premier research institution in basic sciences.
